# Kotlin Ktor Patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor: a Ktor server patterns skill for building Kotlin backends the idiomatic way. It covers the standard project layout (Application entry point, plugins, routes, models, services, repositories, Koin DI modules), the routing DSL, and plugin configuration for the pieces every server needs: authentication, CORS, content negotiation with kotlinx.serialization, error handling with StatusPages, dependency injection with Koin, WebSocket endpoints, and integration tests using testApplication. The guidance is concrete: where each file lives, how modules wire together, and how to test routes without standing up a real server. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; assumes Kotlin and Gradle basics plus a Ktor project scaffold; plugin APIs move between Ktor versions, so check the docs for your version. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
